title: Sales Tax Gross-Up of Open Backorders — Commercial Credit Account Room Payments
content:
**Credit desk note — Commercial Credit Account.** In a room payment, **the open backorder value counted** is grossed up by a sales-tax ratio drawn from the account's own invoices: the value counted is the open backorder value increased by that ratio of itself.

### Clause

The open backorder value counted is grossed up by a sales-tax ratio: on an account billed monthly consolidated that was billed sales tax in the last twelve whole months the ratio is the sales tax to the merchandise subtotal of all invoices dated on the latest invoice date, on an account billed per shipment that was billed sales tax in the last twelve whole months it is the sales tax to the merchandise subtotal billed over those twelve months; on any other account the ratio is zero, and a ratio is zero wherever the merchandise compared is nothing.

The last twelve whole months are the invoices dated less than twelve whole months before today, whole months being the difference in calendar months less one when today's day of the month is earlier than the invoice date's day of the month. The latest invoice date is the latest invoice date on the account.

### Branches

| Billing cycle | Sales tax billed in the last twelve whole months | Ratio |
|---|---|---|
| monthly consolidated | yes | sales tax to merchandise of all invoices dated on the latest invoice date |
| per shipment | yes | sales tax to merchandise of the invoices of the last twelve whole months |
| either | no | zero |

### Example (hypothetical)

A per-shipment account was billed 1200.00 of sales tax on 16000.00 of merchandise in the last twelve whole months: the ratio is 0.075, and open backorders of 4000.00 count as 4300.00.
